info.summary: API for the next gen watsonx Orchestrate stack
info.description:
The watsonx Orchestrate Server provides a set of APIs to power the watsonx Orchestrate AI assistant. This includes the following core services:

* Orchestrate Assistant - a built-in AI assistant that powers the Orchestrate end-user experience.
* Custom Assistants - a service layer for interacting with existing AI assistatns (such as those in watsonx Assistant).
* Message Threads - a chat history and async message tracking store.
* Document Store - manage collections of documents in nearly any format including text, pdf, html and many more.
* Information Extraction - automatically extract clean text and images from any document in the Document Store.  Also extract other useful metadata like questions answered, keywords, and named entities.
* Embedding - generate vector embeddings for text and images in the Document Store.
* Vector Index and Retrieval - automatically index documents with rich metadata for vector search or hybrid search.
* Search Engine - create a Gen AI powered search engine that works like Bing or Google.
* Query Engine - configure your own RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation) engine supporting advanced retrieval patterns and automated data management.
* Model Proxy - create your own LLM model endpoints for chat completions and embeddings.  Supports IBM watsonx.ai, IBM BAM, OpenAI, MistralAI, or Ollama for local models.

WxO API Server utilizes the following open source projects:

* [PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/)
* [PGVector](https://github.com/pgvector/pgvector)
* [LlamaIndex](https://docs.llamaindex.ai/en/stable/)
* [LangChain](https://python.langchain.com/docs/get_started/introduction)
* [FastAPI](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/)
* [Unstructured](https://unstructured.io/)
* [Celery](https://docs.celeryproject.org/en/stable/)

post.description:
Cancel a run — the Redis latch/cancel-key flow is entirely for voice
(is_voice from ``x-communication-type``; other channels skip Redis).

1. Read the run's DB status (tenant-scoped): missing → 404, already
   finished → 409 "cannot cancel". Done before Redis because the busy
   latch is never deleted (TTL expiry only) and outlives the run.
2. Busy latch check: the tool node latches ``<run_id>_<thread_id>`` before
   its first tool call, so an in-flight run is cancellable only before
   that point → 409 busy afterwards.
3. Flip DB status to cancelled (the DAO re-checks the status first), then
   write the ``.._cancel`` presence key. Its only reader is the node-entry
   cancel check (cancel_check.with_cancel_check), so the graph halts at the
   next node boundary. If no boundary remains (answer already streaming),
   the run finishes and the worker's COMPLETED patch overwrites the
   cancelled status — cancel is then accepted but not enforced.

This endpoint orchestrates the execution of an agent architect graph,
handling thread management, checkpointing, and streaming responses.

    request: FastAPI request object

    multiple_content: Whether to handle multiple content types
    stream_timeout: Timeout for streaming in milliseconds
    flag: Feature flag dependency
    
Returns:
    StreamingResponse with event stream
    
Raises:
    HTTPException: For various validation and execution errors
    DataAccessException: For database access errors

Execute Agent Architect v2 with LangGraph integration.

This endpoint provides an enhanced version of the Agent Architect chat interface,
supporting both standard operation procedure (SOP) mode and legacy phase 1 mode.

Args:
    current_user (UserProfile): Authenticated user profile with tenant information.
    session (Session): Database session for data access operations.
    request (Request): FastAPI request object containing HTTP request details.
    run_obj (RunOrchestrate): Orchestration configuration including assistant ID,
        thread ID, and conversation parameters.
    stream (bool, optional): Enable streaming response mode. Defaults to False.
    multiple_content (bool, optional): Support multiple content types in response.
        Defaults to False.
    enable_sop (bool, optional): Enable Standard Operation Procedure (Phase 2) mode.
        When True, uses graph-based agent architect. When False, uses Phase 1 mode.
        Defaults to True.
    stream_timeout (int, optional): Timeout for streaming responses in milliseconds.
        Defaults to 60000 (60 seconds).
    flag: Feature flag dependency for API access control.

Returns:
    Union[StreamingResponse, AssistantRunResponse]: Either a streaming response
        for real-time interaction or a complete assistant run response.

Raises:
    DataAccessException: When database access fails, with appropriate status code.
    HTTPException: For HTTP-related errors during request processing.
    Exception: For unexpected errors, logged with 500 status code.

Note:
    - All exceptions are audited with appropriate action and status codes
    - Phase 2 (SOP mode) is the recommended default for enhanced capabilities
    - Phase 1 mode is maintained for backward compatibility

get.description:
List the watsonx Assistant instances available to the current tenant.

The watsonx Assistant tenant is derived automatically from the caller's
Orchestrate identity, so no CRN is required on the request. Results can
be scoped to a single information architecture or combined across both:

- `new_ia=true` returns assistants from the new IA only.
- `new_ia=false` returns assistants from the legacy IA only.
- `new_ia=both` returns the union, optionally sorted by `sort`.

Pagination is applied server-side; pass `limit` and `offset` to page
through results. When the current tenant has no linked watsonx Assistant
instance, an empty list is returned.

get.description:
Get associated artifacts for an agent to check publishability.

This API analyzes whether the specified agent can be published to the catalog by evaluating
all publishable artifacts (agents and tools) and any blocking components that may prevent publishing.

The API returns:
- Artifact types that are currently supported for publishing
- Publishable artifacts (agents/tools) that are supported for publishing
- Publish blockers that prevent publishing, including:
  - Artifacts with unsupported types
  - Non-artifact components (e.g., knowledge bases, channels, guidelines)

Query Parameters:
- scope (string, optional, default='direct'): Scope of artifacts to retrieve
  - 'direct': Returns only 1st-level artifacts (direct children of the specified agent_id)
  - 'all': Returns all artifacts recursively across all hierarchy levels

Only admins can query associated artifacts.

Bulk import skills from a zip bundle.

Expected zip structure::

    skills-bundle.zip
      bundle-format          <- must contain "skills-2.0.0"
      manifest.json          <- optional; explicitly declares skill paths
      skill-name/
        SKILL.md             <- required per skill

If absent, all ``SKILL.md`` files found anywhere in the zip are imported.

**Upsert behaviour**: if a skill with the same name already exists in the
workspace it is *updated*; otherwise it is *created*.  Running the same
bundle repeatedly is therefore safe and idempotent.

      "imported": [{"name": "...", "id": "...", "action": "created|updated", "scripts": 1}],
      "failed":   [{"name": "...", "error": "..."}],

Upload a script file for a skill.

``skill_id`` accepts either the skill's UUID or its name, e.g.::

    POST /skills/invoice-management/scripts
    POST /skills/3f2504e0-4f89-11d3-9a0c-0305e82c3301/scripts

The script will be stored at:
``skills/{tenant_id}/{skill_name}/{script_path}``

Upload a reference doc for a skill (agentskills.io ``references/``).

``skill_id`` accepts either the skill's UUID or its name, e.g.::

    POST /skills/invoice-management/references
    POST /skills/3f2504e0-4f89-11d3-9a0c-0305e82c3301/references

The file is stored at ``skills/{tenant_id}/{skill_name}/{reference_path}``.

Unlike scripts, references are plain docs read on demand by the agent — any
filename/extension is allowed (REFERENCE.md, finance.txt, lookup.json …),
there is no security gate. The path is tracked in the ``references`` JSONB
column (so the prompt can list them) and the files are stored under
``scripts_storage_path/references/`` (same root as scripts, snapshotted at
release like the scripts folder).

Resolve + fetch a bundled reference doc's text for the caller's tenant.

Resolution (``match_reference``) is tolerant of the path forms models emit.
Returns ``{relpath, content}``; 404 (with the available references) when the
requested path matches none of the active skill's bundled references.

- `total`: Total number of agents matching the search/filter criteria
- `result_count`: Number of agents returned in current page

patch.description:
Updates the schedulable status of an agent.

When scheduling is enabled (is_schedulable=true):
1. Registers Flow Runtime as remote MCP server (tenant-level, one-time)
2. Binds 5 scheduling MCP tools to the specific agent (agent-level)

The MCP server uses Streamable HTTP transport without connection.

Dispatcher-style PATCH for agent identity.
Each recognised field triggers an independent sub-operation.
Multiple fields in one request run in order; results are merged into one response.

Supported fields today:
  enabled=true   → _handle_enable()   — create identity in CM
  enabled=false  → _handle_disable()  — delete identity in CM
  agentOwners    → _handle_owners()   — register owners in IBM Verify (non-fatal)

Scope restriction — native agents only:
  This endpoint uses AgentDAO.find_by_id() which queries the `agents` table only.
  LangGraph (external) agents stored in `ext_assistants` will receive a 404 here.
  External agent identity is provisioned at creation time via ExternalChatAgentDAO
  and cannot be managed via this endpoint post-creation. This is a known v1
  limitation — see follow-up: EPIC-72982 / H-2.

         or a concurrent request created the same next version_label first (agent_version_pkey)

    1. API request level: `settings.max_user_turns` is accepted by this endpoint.

Returns evaluation metrics for agents including:
- **Agent Name**: Display name of each agent
- **Number of Test Cases**: Total count of test cases for the agent (from TestCasesORM)
- **Total Evaluations**: Total number of evaluations (all statuses)
- **Completed Evaluations**: Number of evaluations that ran successfully (status=COMPLETED)
- **Evaluation Success Rate**: Percentage of completed evaluations (completed/total * 100)
- **Last Executed Date**: Finished date of the most recent completed evaluation

**Filtering Options:**
- Filter by workspace ID
- Filter by date range (evaluations within specified period)
- Both start_date and end_date must be provided together

**Sorting:**
- Sorted by last_executed_date
- Sort order: ascending (asc) or descending (desc)

**Pagination:**
- Use limit and offset for result pagination
- Maximum limit: 100 results per page

**Includes All Agents:**
- Returns agents even if they have no evaluations
- Agents without evaluations show 0 for counts and NULL for last executed date

**Examples:**
- All agents: `GET /v1/orchestrate/dashboard/analytics/agents/evaluations`
- Workspace filter: `GET /v1/orchestrate/dashboard/analytics/agents/evaluations?workspace_id=xxx`
- Date range: `GET /v1/orchestrate/dashboard/analytics/agents/evaluations?start_date=2026-04-01T00:00:00Z&end_date=2026-04-30T23:59:59Z`
- Sort ascending: `GET /v1/orchestrate/dashboard/analytics/agents/evaluations?sort_order=asc`
- Combined filters: `GET /v1/orchestrate/dashboard/analytics/agents/evaluations?workspace_id=xxx&start_date=2026-04-01T00:00:00Z&end_date=2026-04-30T23:59:59Z&sort_order=desc&limit=50`

**Response:**
Returns a paginated list with:
- `agent_id`: Agent UUID
- `agent_name`: Agent name
- `agent_display_name`: Agent display name

get.description:
Get paginated list of agents with comprehensive analytics metrics.

This endpoint provides a summary view of all agents with their key performance metrics:
- Total user messages sent to the agent
- Total unique conversations/sessions
- Total failed assistant runs
- Total unique active users who interacted with the agent
- Total evaluation runs for the agent

**Features:**
- Pagination support with configurable limit/offset
- Optional date range filtering for metrics
- Case-insensitive partial search by agent name
- Flexible sorting by any metric or agent property
- Workspace filtering

**Date Filtering:**
- Both `start_date` and `end_date` are optional
- If not provided, returns all-time metrics
- If provided, both must be specified together
- Dates must be in ISO 8601 format (e.g., 2026-04-01T10:00:00Z)
- Date filters apply to all metrics (messages, conversations, failed runs, users, evaluations)

**Sorting Options:**
- `total_messages_desc` (default): Most active agents first
- `total_messages_asc`: Least active agents first
- `total_conversations_desc/asc`: Sort by conversation count
- `total_active_users_desc/asc`: Sort by unique user count
- `updated_at_desc/asc`: Sort by last update time
- `name_asc/desc`: Sort alphabetically by agent name

**Note:** Sorting by `total_failed_messages` is not supported as failed traces
are fetched from the analytics API after the database query.

**Examples:**

1. Get top 20 most active agents (all time):
   ```
   GET /v1/orchestrate/dashboard/analytics/agents/summary
   ```

2. Search for agents with "support" in name, sorted by messages:
   ```
   GET /v1/orchestrate/dashboard/analytics/agents/summary?agent_name=support&sort_by=total_messages_desc
   ```

3. Get agents with metrics for March 2026:
   ```
   GET /v1/orchestrate/dashboard/analytics/agents/summary?start_date=2026-03-01T00:00:00Z&end_date=2026-03-31T23:59:59Z
   ```

4. Get agents in specific workspace, sorted by active users:
   ```
   GET /v1/orchestrate/dashboard/analytics/agents/summary?workspace_id=xxx&sort_by=total_active_users_desc
   ```

5. Paginate through results:
   ```
   GET /v1/orchestrate/dashboard/analytics/agents/summary?limit=50&offset=0
   GET /v1/orchestrate/dashboard/analytics/agents/summary?limit=50&offset=50
   ```

**Response:**
Returns a paginated response with:
- `data`: List of agent analytics summaries
- `total`: Total count of agents matching filters
- `limit`: Results per page
- `offset`: Number of results skipped
- `result_count`: Number of results in current page
- `timeframe_start`: Start of analysis period (null if not filtered)
- `timeframe_end`: End of analysis period (null if not filtered)

get.summary: Get analytics on all available models and their usage by agents
get.description:
Get analytics on which models are being used by agents.

This endpoint returns statistics showing which LLM models are currently in use
across agents, along with the count of agents using each model. This is useful
for understanding model adoption patterns, usage distribution, and identifying
the most popular models in your organization.

**Features:**
- Lists all unique models currently assigned to agents
- Shows agent count per model
- Includes model display names when available
- Optional workspace filtering
- Results ordered by agent count (most used first)

**Use Cases:**
- Display model usage distribution in charts/dashboards
- Identify most popular models for capacity planning
- Track model adoption across teams/workspaces
- Understand model diversity in your agent ecosystem

**Query Parameters:**
- `workspace_id` (optional): Filter results to a specific workspace. If omitted,
  returns model usage across all workspaces the user has access to.

**Response:**
Returns a `ModelAnalyticsResponse` containing:
- `total_models`: Total number of unique models in use
- `total_agents`: Total number of agents analyzed (with models assigned)
- `models`: List of model usage summaries, each containing:
    - `model_id`: The model identifier (e.g., "watsonx/meta-llama/llama-3-405b-instruct")
    - `model_name`: Human-readable model name (if available from model registry)
    - `agent_count`: Number of agents using this model
    - `tags`: List of model tags (if available from model registry)
    - `lifecycle`: List of lifecycle status information (if available from OOTB models config)

**Example Request:**
```
GET /orchestrate/dashboard/model-usage
GET /orchestrate/dashboard/model-usage?workspace_id=123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000
```

**Example Response:**
```json
{
    "total_models": 3,
    "total_agents": 25,
    "models": [
        {
            "model_id": "watsonx/meta-llama/llama-3-405b-instruct",
            "model_name": "Llama 3 405B Instruct",
            "agent_count": 15,
            "tags": ["watsonx", "llama"],
            "lifecycle": [{"id": "available", "label": "Available"}]
        },
        {
            "model_id": "groq/openai/gpt-oss-120b",
            "model_name": "GPT-OSS 120B",
            "agent_count": 8,
            "tags": ["groq"],
            "lifecycle": []
        },
        {
            "model_id": "watsonx/meta-llama/llama-3-2-90b-vision-instruct",
            "model_name": "Llama 3.2 90B Vision",
            "agent_count": 2,
            "tags": ["watsonx", "vision"],
            "lifecycle": [{"id": "available", "label": "Available"}]
        }
    ]
}
```

**Notes:**
- Only includes agents with a model assigned (non-null `llm` field)
- Excludes deleted agents
- Model names and tags are fetched from the model registry when available
- Lifecycle information is fetched from OOTB models configuration when available
- Results are ordered by agent count in descending order
